title: Contracts that do what they say
overseerSummary: The six move to a 'not implemented' table so they are kept as data; the three real ones keep today's frequency. Pay drops on affected contracts and the card figure becomes reproducible from what is on screen.

proposals.title: Make contract complications real data, hold their frequency, and make the payout figure checkable
proposals.problem: The contract board lists complications with a described effect and a reward multiplier of x1.15 to x1.6. Six of the nine (Storm, Reinforcements, Infested, Hunted, Turncoat, A trap) have no code behind them, and every one of them still multiplies the payout. Measured over 3000 rolls per level with types drawn uniformly: 12.1% of level-1 contracts, 25.1% of level-10 contracts and 41.7% of level-20 contracts carry at least one inert twist. The card shows only 'x2.76 gems'. That reads as a multiplier on gems, the base is not on screen and the factors are not itemised, so the player cannot check it. Night's text promises 'patrols walk shorter circuits', which no code does. The overtime log line prints 'still paying' with no figure while three other places print +N%.
evidence: missiontypes.js:812-831 TWISTS: nine entries (label, weight, reward, optional only/not, desc). Only three have consumers: field.js:2051 (night: sight 9 becomes Math.round(9/2) = 5), sortie.js:371 (dry: no regen), field.js:1531 (hardcore: canEscalate). grep -w for storm, infested, hunted, turncoat, reinforcements finds each id only at its own row; the twist id 'trap' appears nowhere else (field.js:1795-1811 'trap' is a structure kind, unrelated).
missiontypes.js:815 Night desc says 'patrols walk shorter circuits'; grep for 'circuit' in all .js finds no consumer.

Scratchpad run cleanup2/twist.js (3000 rolls per level): contracts with at least one inert twist 12.1/18.0/25.1/35.1/41.7% at levels 1/5/10/15/20; mean reward multiplier 1.158 with all twists vs 1.064 counting only the three live ones at level 10 (1.260 vs 1.107 at level 20).

missiontypes.js:857-870 rollTwists: a draw succeeds with probability odds (0.2..0.6 by level, x0.35 per further draw), then weightedPick over what remains. Simulation cleanup2/twist2.js (60000 rolls): with the six rows deleted and nothing else changed, hardcore goes from 5.4% to 13.0% of level-10 contracts and from 9.2% to 22.2% at level 20.
missiontypes.js:959 reward = round2(spec.reward x product of TWISTS[id].reward over every rolled twist, inert or not).

sortie.js:479 worth = round((25 + level*30) x m.reward x sideMult x (1+over) x (escaped ? 0.35 : 1)); the constants 25, 30 and 0.35 exist only in settle(). sortie.js:482-486 resource payout: N/12 each of crops, ore, herbs plus 25% of N as gems.
sortie.js:783-784 the card prints each twist label with title = desc, then the tag 'x{m.reward} {m.payout}'.

Offers are persisted in three places that can hold a removed twist id: gs.field.board (sortie.js:95-102), a run in progress (saved mission, sortie.js:312 resume), and trial offers state.trials rolled by MT.roll (quests.js:109-121). missiontypes.js:1043 describe() does TWISTS[id].label with no guard; field.js:2071 and sortie.js:783 do the same, so a saved 'storm' throws on render.
sortie.js:434 overtimePay; sortie.js:481, 1307, 1310 print '+N%'; field.js:1419 prints '...held past the terms, and still paying' with no figure.
missiontypes.js:777 SIDE_JOBS.plunder.on contains 'ruins' and missiontypes.js:823 hunted.not contains 'arena'; neither is a TYPES key (those are map ids).
proposals.change:
1) TWISTS keeps night, dry, hardcore and gives each its effect as data: night mods { sight: 0.5 }, dry mods { regen: 0 }, hardcore mods { escalates: true }. The six inert rows move into a comment block under the table, headed 'not implemented: needs a mods entry and one consumer', with their label, weight, reward, only/not and desc, so the authored ideas are kept and re-adding one is a table row plus one consumer line. Nothing the code reads lists them. New MT.modsOf(mission) folds the known twists' mods (defaults sight 1, regen 1, escalates false) and MT.twistOf(id) returns null for an unknown id. Consumers: field.js:2051 sight = Math.round(MT.SIGHT * mods.sight) (SIGHT moves from field.js:69 to MT so the text and the code share it), sortie.js:371 REGEN * mods.regen, field.js:1531 mods.escalates. The tooltip text is generated from the mods by a MOD_TEXT table: 'Sight 5 tiles instead of 9, both sides'; 'No hp or pool recovery between fights'; 'A failed objective or an overrun clock changes the job to extraction: hostile groups +50%, alarm raised, an escape pays x0.35'. The +50% (field.js:1553) and x0.35 (sortie.js:479) become MT.ESCALATION_SPAWN and MT.PAYOUT.escape, read by both the code and the text. Night's 'shorter circuits' sentence disappears because the text is no longer hand-written.
2) Hold frequency. rollTwists replaces R.chance(odds) with R.chance(odds * min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL)) with TWIST_FULL = 66, so a given twist is drawn with probability odds x weight / 66 regardless of how many other rows exist. Measured with the three rows (cleanup2/twist2.js, 60000 rolls): level 10 night/dry/hardcore 8.0/6.8/5.7% against today's live-only 7.6/7.6/5.4%; level 20 13.0/11.0/9.5% against 12.9/12.6/9.2%. Adding a twist later adds its own draw probability and leaves the others unchanged until the weights sum to 66.
3) Old saves. MT.current(m) is true when every twist id is known. The board getter (sortie.js:95-102) filters the board with it and Quests.offer (quests.js:109) treats a held offer that fails it as absent and re-rolls (both re-roll anyway: the board every 6 minutes, trial pairs for free). resume (sortie.js:312) keeps the run and its contracted reward; every reader (describe, field.js:2071, sortie.js:783) skips ids for which MT.twistOf is null.
4) Payout in one place. MT.PAYOUT = { base: 25, perLevel: 30, escape: 0.35, bonus: 0.2, resourceGems: 0.25, resourceDiv: 12 } and MT.payout(m, { sideMult = 1, over = 0, escaped = false }) returning { worth, gems, each }. sortie.js:479-495 calls it; the card calls it with the defaults. roll() (missiontypes.js:959) stops rounding reward to 2 decimals so the itemised factors multiply to exactly what pays; displays round.
5) Card (sortie.js:783-784): 'x2.76 gems' becomes 'pays about 747 gems + loot' (resource contracts: 'about E crops, E ore, E herbs, G gems'). The tag title itemises the figure: '25 + 30 x level 10 = 325 / Siege x2.0 / Night x1.15 = 747'. MT.factors(m) returns that list from m.type, m.variant and the known twists. The figure is contract pay only; the label says loot is extra, so it stays true if a loot multiplier lands elsewhere.
6) overtimePay moves next to MT.PORTAL as MT.overtimePay(mission, overtime); sortie.js:434-436 and field.js:1419 both use it, and the log line becomes '...held past the terms: +N% on the contract'.
7) Delete 'ruins' from SIDE_JOBS.plunder.on (missiontypes.js:777); the 'arena' reference goes with the removed hunted row.
8) New test/contracts.js: every TWISTS entry has a non-empty mods object and a MOD_TEXT line for each key; rollTwists never returns an id without mods; for 200 random MT.roll contracts, MT.payout(m) equals the old sortie.js:479 expression; MT.factors(m) multiplies to m.reward; a mission with an unknown twist id fails MT.current and does not throw in describe().
proposals.playerEffect: A complication on the board now does something in the run, and the figure beside the card can be reproduced from things on screen: base for the level, the type multiplier, one multiplier per complication. Today roughly one level-10 contract in four advertises an effect that never happens and pays extra for it. Complications that remain keep the chance they had.
proposals.secondOrder: Mean contract pay falls by 8.1% at level 10 and 12.1% at level 20 (mean multiplier 1.158 to 1.064 and 1.260 to 1.107), so any gem-income tuning that assumed the old board (gemGoal in game.js, town level pacing) gets slightly less. Hardcore and Night keep their frequency, so death rate from escalation does not move. MT.modsOf becomes the one place the other builders add a field effect: a twist is a table row, a MOD_TEXT line and one consumer. MT.payout and MT.PAYOUT are the place a loot or debrief multiplier plugs in without the card drifting from settle().
proposals.risks: Deleting authored content: kept in a comment block, not data. TWIST_FULL = 66 is calibrated by simulation against the pools that exist today (night is illegal in dungeon and duel, hardcore in duel, so per-type pools differ); it is a documented constant, not derived. The legacy filter must be applied at all three load points or a saved 'storm' throws on render. Not unique to this change: it shares missiontypes.js text and the card with cleanup-register-pass, so one owner applies this first and that one second. No harness regex or test reads twists (grep of test/ for 'twist' is empty).
proposals.response: Design attack (silent economy change, survivors 2.5x more frequent): accepted. Frequency is held by dividing the draw probability by 66 and measured above; the pay drop is stated as a number, not hidden. Design demand to cut Night's text to what field.js:2051 does: accepted, the text is now generated from the mods. Engineering demand to keep the six rows with mods null: accepted in intent, rejected in form. Rows left in TWISTS make TWISTS[id] succeed for ids that never fire, which is the lookup that currently lets a typo or legacy id carry a reward multiplier, so they live in a comment block and re-adding is still one row. Engineering demand for the card to say 'before class loot': the card says pays about N gems + loot, contract pay only. Engineering demand for one owner with register-pass: stated in risks; honesty lands first. I added a third persistence point both attackers missed (trial offers in quests.js:109) and made trial offers re-roll rather than keep an inflated reward.

verdicts.attack: It deletes six pieces of authored content instead of implementing them, and because rollTwists draws by odds and then picks from whatever pool is left (missiontypes.js:857-870), the survivors become about 2.5x more frequent: hardcore goes from 4.8% to 13.2% of level-10 contracts in my run, an economy and difficulty change hidden inside a cleanup. Mean payout at level 10 drops about 8%.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS missiontypes.js:812-831; consumers only field.js:1531 (hardcore), 2051 (night), sortie.js:371 (dry); grep finds storm/infested/hunted/turncoat/reinforcements only at their definitions; reward product at 959; card at sortie.js:783-784; payout constants only at sortie.js:479; 'ruins' (777) and 'arena' (823) are not TYPES keys; Night's 'patrols walk shorter circuits' has no code (grep circuit). My 3000-roll sample: inert share 11.5/24.2/41.7% at levels 1/10/20, multiplier ratio 1.083 at level 10, hardcore 4.8% to 13.2% after deleting the six, all matching the builder's figures.
verdicts.demand: Hold hardcore and the other survivors at today's frequency (scale odds at missiontypes.js:862). Legacy-id filter at both load points (sortie.js:97-102 and 317). Night's description reduced to what field.js:2051 does. The card's 'about N gems' computed by the same MT.payout that settle() uses. The harness regexes unaffected.

verdicts.attack: It deletes six authored complications the file header (missiontypes.js:25) plainly intends to implement; after deletion hardcore's share of twist draws rises about 2.5x (weight 9 of 33 instead of 9 of 84) at the same draw odds, which is an economy and death-rate change. It collides with cleanup-register-pass on the same card, tooltips and field.js:1419, and with systems-one-debrief's loot multiplier on the 'about N gems' figure.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified TWISTS at missiontypes.js:812-831; the only consumers are field.js:1531 (hardcore), 2051 (night), sortie.js:371 (dry); reward product at 959; the card at sortie.js:783-784; payout at 479; '+N%' at 434/481/1307 vs 'still paying' at field.js:1419; 'ruins' (777) and 'arena' (823) are not TYPES keys (keys at missiontypes.js:332-718); the board is persisted (sortie.js:97-102) and missiontypes.js:1043 describe() would throw on an unknown id. Sampling percentages not re-run.
verdicts.demand: 1) Keep the six rows with mods: null and have rollTwists draw only twists with a non-empty mods object, so re-adding one is data. 2) Hold the per-draw odds so hardcore frequency is unchanged, and state before/after at levels 10 and 20. 3) The card says 'about N gems before class loot' once systems-one-debrief lands. 4) One owner with register-pass for sortie.js:768-787, field.js:1419 and missiontypes.js text.
